clue.text: Port with fowl or fish, surprisingly

parts.note: Bombay (now Mumbai) is a major Indian port
a duck is a kind of fowl

explanation.surface: A dish of harbour-town poultry, or perhaps fish, offered as a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surprise is that something called a duck is in fact a fish, so 'surprisingly' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay duck is a small lizardfish of South Asia, usually eaten dried, which is unexpected given its bird name.

clue.text: Having full employment in vehicle factory, finally

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word factory

explanation.surface: A car plant where every worker has a job, at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fully occupied with work has no spare time, which is being occupied.

clue.text: Religious symbol seen in Buddhist city, endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the city's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Mandalay is a city in Myanmar, a centre of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A sacred emblem spotted all over a Burmese temple city.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandala is a circular diagram symbolising the universe in Hindu and Buddhist ritual.

clue.text: Expert finished successfully

explanation.surface: A specialist completed the job with success.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled, gifted performer is masterly; a task carried through to the end has been achieved.

clue.text: Oust head of department with special order

indicators.note: head of asks for the leading letter of the word department
putting the letters of special in a new order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A department chief is removed by a special decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a noun meaning a decree, which suits the surface, but here it is the instruction to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To displace someone is to push them out of their position, a synonym of expel.

clue.text: Post that's filled by journalist

explanation.surface: A job vacancy that a reporter takes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar or upright support is one sense; the other is a regular newspaper feature space a writer must fill.

clue.text: Eldest son a ruse deprived of right, despicably

indicators.note: despicably suggests the remaining letters behave badly and are scrambled
deprived of says a letter is taken away from the words a ruse

explanation.surface: A firstborn cheated of his birthright by a contemptible trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from A RUSE leaves AUSE, which 'despicably' rearranges. Fittingly, Esau was tricked out of his birthright by Jacob.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau is the elder twin son of Isaac, who lost his birthright to Jacob.

clue.text: Warden, a self-styled bird-watcher?

explanation.surface: The head of a college describes himself as an avid birder.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner was Warden of New College, Oxford, famous for slips swapping the starts of words; the question mark flags the playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: William Spooner was Warden of New College, Oxford; one famous for swapping word beginnings might call a bird-watcher a 'word-botcher'.

clue.text: Twig found beneath area of growing trees

parts.note: beneath means under
a stand is a group of growing trees

explanation.surface: A small branch discovered under a copse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like a bit of a tree, matching the surface, but here it is the informal verb meaning to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal British for to grasp or realise something.

clue.text: Building on the Strand where Englishman lives with authoress

parts.note: George Sand was a French novelist
the saying goes that an Englishman's home is his castle

explanation.surface: A house on a London street where an Englishman lives with a woman writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Strand' looks like the London street, but here it means the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand is an old word for beach, and a sculpted heap of beach grains is what children build there.

clue.text: All the wise need is intelligence

explanation.surface: Sensible people only need some brains.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a hint to the wise is enough; and news or information is another sense.

clue.text: Entertainment we get from France, in two senses

definitions.text: Entertainment we get from France, in two senses

parts.words: Entertainment we get from France, in two senses
parts.note: a French night-time show whose name means sound and light, appealing to hearing and sight

explanation.surface: A French show that appeals two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: This open-air spectacle of lighting and recorded narration at a historic site originated in France.

clue.text: Tree in square

explanation.surface: A tree planted in a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a tropical fronded plant; the other is to bribe, as square also means.

clue.text: Satirist wanting to strike political leaders a heavy blow

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or strike
the leading letters of the word political
a oner is old slang for a heavy blow

explanation.surface: A satirist keen to land a punch on politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ridicules people in mocking writing is a mocker or parodist.

clue.text: City editor forced to go on board

parts.note: Shanghai is a Chinese city

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor in a Chinese port is made to board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors were once kidnapped and pressed into a ship's crew, named after the Chinese port.

clue.text: Possibly hold cake in this —- or loaf

definitions.text: Possibly hold cake in this —- or loaf

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of hold and cake can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Where you might keep a cake, or a loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HOLD and CAKE together are all 'in this'; 'loaf' is slang for the head, the part a wrestler grips.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip that clamps the opponent's head under the arm is a hold, and loaf is slang for head.

clue.text: Prayer and religious education in nonconformist group

indicators.note: in places religious education inside the group

parts.note: a sect is a dissenting religious group
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: Worship and scripture lessons within a breakaway church.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Latin Mass the Secret is the prayer said quietly by the priest after the offertory.

clue.text: Raised voice in current argument

parts.note: the Fal is a Cornish river, and a river is a current
a set-to is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Shouting during a topical row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an adjective (topical) but it is a river, the Fal in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing voice pitched above the natural range, as by male singers, is a heightened register.

clue.text: One who's barely acceptable in colony

definitions.text: One who's barely acceptable in colony

parts.words: One who's barely acceptable in colony
parts.note: in a naturist community only someone wearing nothing is welcome, playing on barely as unclothed

explanation.surface: Someone only just tolerated in a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist lives without clothes, the only acceptable state in such a colony.

clue.text: Daughter is embraced by designer in art school

indicators.note: embraced by puts is inside the designer

parts.note: Robert Adam was a famous Scottish architect and designer

explanation.surface: A girl is hugged by a fashion designer at art college.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an early twentieth-century anti-art movement, a school of artistic thought.

clue.text: Laura's skirts in woollen fabric, or cotton

indicators.note: in places those edge letters inside the fabric

parts.note: tartan is a checked woollen cloth

indicators.note: skirts are the edges, so the outside letters of Laura

explanation.surface: Laura's skirts come in plaid wool or in cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like garments but means borders: Laura's first and last letters L and A go inside TARTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarlatan is a thin stiffened muslin, a fabric woven from cotton.

clue.text: Vehicle a traveller ran into overturned

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned turns the whole run upside down

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
to meet is to run into, so met

explanation.surface: A car carrying a salesman crashes and flips over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' is a painting medium, not a car. A, REP and MET joined give AREPMET, which 'overturned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: In painting, a vehicle is the binding medium, and egg yolk is the classic one for this method.

clue.text: Oxford policeman apprehends old blue

indicators.note: apprehends, like an arrest, holds old inside the detective

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the fictional Oxford detective

explanation.surface: An Oxford detective arrests an elderly Oxford rowing blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like an Oxford sportsman (a university blue) but means gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means sad and sullen, which is the mood of a sulky person.

clue.text: Flies low to reduce risks with short flights

parts.note: to hedge is to protect yourself against loss
hops are short trips by air

explanation.surface: A cautious pilot keeps the trips short and low.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot who skims close to the ground clears only the hedgerows, crop-dusting style.

clue.text: It could he a note with brief minutes put round

definitions.text: It could he a note with brief minutes put round

parts.words: It could he a note with brief minutes put round
parts.note: an office note circulated, giving short minutes of a meeting to colleagues

explanation.surface: A note summarising a meeting is sent round.
explanation.definitionFit: A short office message circulated among staff is a memorandum, shortened.

clue.text: To slide, pole needs a little butter.

parts.note: S is the south pole
a butter is something that butts, so a young goat or kid

explanation.surface: A pole on a greasy kitchen floor slides on a bit of butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but something that butts; a little one is a young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle or foot slipping sideways out of control is sliding.

clue.text: River-bird again spotted on island

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places one piece after the other

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music to mean repeat

explanation.surface: A waterbird seen once more on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-billed wading bird, sacred in ancient Egypt, lives by rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Courage and audacity in a tight situation

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck means cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: Bravery and cheek in a tight corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point where flow is restricted, like traffic jams, is a constriction.

clue.text: Foreign council rejected French writer's conclusion

indicators.note: rejected says a letter is thrown out

parts.note: Alexandre Dumas was a French novelist

indicators.note: conclusion picks the last letter of the writer's name

parts.note: Alexandre Dumas was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A council abroad turned down a French author's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duma is the Russian parliament or assembly.

clue.text: Take place prior to action in court, or sooner

indicators.note: prior to puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: to be is to exist or happen
a forehand is a stroke on a tennis court

explanation.surface: Something happens before a legal case, or even earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action in court' looks legal but is a tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier or in advance is a synonym of before the time.
